commit.message:
prove-your-work: drop the caller name from the ledger clause

The layer law says a skill names only skills below its own layer, and
prove-your-work declares no siblings — yet its ledger clause named
`build`, its caller. The edge already lives where it belongs: build's
pipeline says it hands the ledger over. The clause now says "the
invoking workflow hands over", so any workflow can invoke this skill
without the text implying one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Spec location has one home: to-spec's contract, resolved via the registered index

to-spec's fallback contract said docs/specs/<name>.md; to-slices' copy
had drifted to .html (introduced in the #137 rename), and code-review
hunted the path independently — three statements of one contract, two
of them disagreeing.

to-spec stays the producer authority and already registers the specs
location in the project instruction file's ## Context documents index.
Consumers now resolve through that registration instead of restating
path and format: to-slices reads the fallback per to-spec's contract,
code-review's search order names the registered specs location. The
retired 'superseding' wording in synthesis.md becomes the capstone
parentage CONTEXT.md defines. code-review probe P3's search-order
paraphrase reconciled; its quoted key text is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

backlog: the claim gate lives where its knobs are set

The build paragraph restated § Build concurrency and § Quota awareness
near-verbatim — queue semantics, unknown-never-estimated, the no-
downgrade rule — so every gate change (#186, #191) was a three-surface
synchronized edit. The policy playbook is the declared home of the
knobs and already carries every rule; SKILL.md now carries the reading
discipline instead: at each entry into the mark-prepare-dispatch
sequence, apply those two sections. The outcome-accounting restatement
shrinks to its pointer the same way.

Probes P22-P24 re-key to the policy template's own sentences — the
surface consumer repos actually install and dispatched sessions
actually read — with the template named in-context per the probe
header's bundled-reference rule.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

One wake ladder: supervision defers to to-subagent's contract by name

Understanding a silent build took three modules: to-subagent owns the
wake ladder, the bounded watch, and the audit-before-redispatch
Recovery invariant; backlog paraphrased the ledger and the audit in
its own words, and watch-until restated the never-poll rung as its
own doctrine. The invariants now have one home. backlog's supervision
keeps what is genuinely its own — tracker-as-ledger events, deadline
sizing, resume reconciliation — and names to-subagent's Recovery
contract for silence and death; watch-until's rung 1 keeps its
behavior and cites the never-poll rule instead of restating it.
Probe keys P8 (backlog) and P3 (watch-until) re-keyed to the new
sentences.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Teardown order has one owner: worktree Remove; callers keep the when

The environment-then-working-copy order, the from-inside rule, and
dirty refusal are worktree Remove's — enforced by its script and
probed in its own evals — yet backlog restated them at both teardown
sites and merge-changes step 7 restated the full order with its own
rationale. Callers now keep only what is theirs: when teardown
happens (abort, merge, sweep), the user-confirmation judgment on
dirty trees, and branch disposition (deletion after working-copy
removal, verified by query — merge-changes' own capability, since
worktree leaves the branch to its lifecycle owner). The order's
rationale keeps its playbook home in the environment template's
teardown row. Probe keys P9 (backlog) and P4 (merge-changes)
re-keyed; the order-violation fail conditions now bind through the
worktree seam.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

interview deepens with an engine mode; shape shrinks to routing

shape needed a non-interactive interview, and since interview's
interface only offered the interactive loop, shape re-implemented the
frontier mechanics in its own text — compute-the-frontier, tagged
questions, recommended answers: interview's implementation vocabulary
restated across the seam. interview now carries the mode itself:
record in, tagged frontier out as the deliverable, answers back in,
empty-frontier as the engine's done with confirmation left to the
dispatching thread. shape keeps only what is its own — dispatching
engines, combining frontiers into one round, routing answers back —
and its loop bullet stops glossing interview's method. shape probe P9
re-keyed to the new sentences.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

AC-id contract: to-spec's statement is canonical, the copy says so

The criterion-id semantics — stable ids, amend in place, append never
renumber, the builder/verifier/reviewer/evidence keying — lived as
unmarked near-verbatim twins in to-spec's and to-slices' template
guides, so a semantics change was a hand-synchronized edit nobody's
tooling knew about. Per the copy-a-technique convention the to-slices
copy now carries its Adapted-from provenance naming to-spec's
statement as canonical, making the sync deliberate. The consumers
(verify-your-work, code-review, prove-your-work) already key by thin
one-line references and are untouched — the audit of real runs found
the semantics themselves sound, so nothing semantic moves. Also
de-names to-slices in to-spec's ordering note ('downstream splitters'),
its one consumer-naming seal break.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

serve-via-tailnet: drop the annotated serve; plain viewing is the whole skill

The annotation surface (review-server, review-await, chrome, hub) was rarely
used and is no longer needed. The skill now serves an artifact in place for
viewing and reports the URL with its stop command — nothing bundled. Playbook
and convention examples that pointed at review-server.py now point at the
worktree skill's script; the site manifest and probes follow.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The skill can now trigger implicitly in both harnesses (invocation: model,
allow_implicit_invocation: true). What survives everywhere it's mentioned is
the real rule — never the default presentation path — with the caller
restriction dropped from the playbooks and templates that stated it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The detail doc carries full rationale and before/after tables.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

New reference skill: outside-in — the shaping decision-ordering standard

Users → experience → system behavior → implementation, worked as a gradient: the user-type roster as a context-file fact, the tree law (implementation enters the frontier only under settled behavior), the seam as a named handoff point, recommend-don't-ask in the implementation register, register skipping, per-register blessing against the spec hash. Wired into shape (tree building, seam, per-register blessing), to-spec (register-ordered sections), and backlog groom (routing partially blessed subjects). Interview stays sealed — the doctrine lives at the shaping layer.

Also: the push-early discipline — commits on work/feature/artifact branches reach the remote as they land (AGENTS.md convention + platform template binding); pushing is backup, publication is the change request.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Rename outside-in → experience-first

The name is the rule: every affected user type's experience, then system behavior, then implementation. Wide enough for operators and API consumers where UX-first would re-narrow to screens.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Blessing invalidation is per covered text, not per commit

A later commit reopens a blessing only when it changes the text that blessing covers — the register's sections for a register blessing, the whole spec otherwise; the check is a diff between the blessed hash and the head. Without this, every implementation commit would reopen the experience blessing and per-register blessing would be useless.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Split the writing standard: unslop, writing-for-humans, technical-writing

writing-for-humans straddled two registers with conflicting rules:
conversational voice (vary rhythm, let mess in) and artifact uniformity
(STE-style discipline). Split by register instead:

- unslop: the shared AI-tell scan, our pinned rewrite of Cursor pstack's
- writing-for-humans: conversation only; voice plus the Provost rhythm
  quote (em dash edited to a comma per our punctuation rule)
- technical-writing: durable artifacts; distills ASD-STE100 and Google
  developer style, adapted from Cursor pstack's technical-writing

Both standards require unslop and degrade in one line without it.
AGENTS.md and CONTEXT.md now route by register; sibling skills still
cite writing-for-humans and get re-routed in a follow-up.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

to-thread) keep writing-for-humans. requires/optional records updated to

The installed external unslop is removed: the family now ships its own

README install instructions now mount the entire family via one
copy-paste command, the agent prompt points at it, and AGENTS.md gains
the rule that keeps those lists in sync with skills/. Catalog gains
unslop and technical-writing rows and drops the stale
writing-technical-docs row.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Restructure the lifecycle family around GitHub, one playbook, and verb skills

Fix the platform to GitHub issues and PRs via gh, git, and an S3-compatible
bucket, and collapse the playbooks to docs/agents/environment.md. Backlog
becomes a thin dispatcher whose verbs (capture, groom, build, retro, status,
setup) each fan one run of a verb skill per unit: capture (was to-backlog),
shape, deliver (was build-change), retro (promoted from in-progress), with
merge (was merge-change) as the human gate. Labels, claims, deadlines, and
branch names are fixed in backlog/reference/labels.md.

Shape commits every artifact to one artifact/<issue> branch and runs
to-slices at the close; to-slices publishes ready sub-issues that block the
spec issue; deliver gains the four issue kinds and the spec issue's coverage
check and promotion PR; merge closes children at their spec-branch merge and
folds in watch-until. Verification splits checks into guards and throwaway
scripts and treats the seed as a claim; the stage ledger is dropped.

skill-loop leaves the install, to-tailnet moves to personal, watch-until is
removed. Sidecars, READMEs, the catalog, CONTEXT.md, AGENTS.md, and the
changelog follow.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Ship a dark, Vercel-inspired default skin for diagram-design

The shipped visual system flips to dark by default: true-black paper,
near-white ink, a neutral gray ramp for muted, soft, and rules, and one
blue accent (#0070f3) with a low-saturation blue for link arrows. Light
is now the alternate variant. style-guide.md defines both columns and
the inversion rule; every type reference, primitive, and template
carries the new hex values, the "Dark mode" sections become "Light
mode", and the tint alphas sit higher on the dark column. The semantic
override palette lists the dark-legible hexes and light mode darkens
them (C_dark), reversing the old C_light rule. Contrast figures cited
in the bar, line, scatter, and treemap references are recomputed for
the new tokens.

template-dark.html becomes template-light.html; the variant slug suffix
is -light. The pre-baked example assets keep the upstream skin and are
documented as layout references only. Credits and changelog record the
reskin.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Read the diagram-design skin off Vercel's Geist scales

Replace the guessed dark tokens with values from the published Geist
color scales: paper is background-100 (#0a0a0a) not pure black, raised
node and card surfaces are gray-100 (#1a1a1a), hairlines stay at the
gray-alpha-400 alpha, and text keeps gray-900/1000. The accent moves
from the saturated blue-700 button fill to the blue-900 text step
(#52a8ff dark, #0068d6 light), which is what Geist uses for text,
icons, and strokes, and link arrows take blue-700 so they sit below
the focal element in brightness. The series and semantic override
palettes use each hue's 900 step with light-mode counterparts, and the
light variant takes those steps instead of darkening arithmetically.

Chip text drops from weight 700 to 600, contrast figures cited in the
bar, line, scatter, and treemap references are recomputed for the new
paper, and the style guide gains a reading-comfort rule.
